findings.evidence: Lines 95–101 only form `AddSubgroup.closure (Set.range (Ring.choose r))`; Mathlib defines `Ring.choose` at `Mathlib/RingTheory/Binomial.lean:380` under `[AddCommGroupWithOne R] [Pow R ℕ] [BinomialRing R]`, and `choose_zero_right` at line 410 adds only `[NatPowAssoc R]`.
findings.fix: State the first two under `[AddCommGroupWithOne R] [Pow R ℕ] [BinomialRing R]`, adding `[NatPowAssoc R]` only for `one_mem_ringChooseSpan`; retain `[Ring R]` for the multiplicative subring results.
findings.issue: `ringChooseSpan` and `ringChoose_mem_ringChooseSpan` inherit `[Ring R]`, although neither uses multiplication; `one_mem_ringChooseSpan` likewise only needs power compatibility.

summary: The additive-span API is unnecessarily restricted to associative rings despite using only the weaker assumptions of Mathlib’s `Ring.choose` API.
